story_type: solid rocket booster static test fire
hook: Four million pounds of thrust, and it never moved an inch.
narration: This rocket booster pushed with more than four million pounds of thrust, lying on its side.
It is a new solid rocket motor, built for future flights of NASA's Moon rocket.
On June twenty sixth, 2025, it was fired in the Utah desert, held down by a giant block of concrete.
Once a solid rocket motor is lit, nobody can throttle it or switch it off. It burns until the fuel is gone.
This one had more than one point four million pounds of propellant to get through.
[short pause] Partway through the burn, chunks of debris blew out of the fire near the nozzle.
And the motor kept roaring, while sensors tracked hundreds of measurements on seven hundred sixty three channels of data.
outcome: It burned for about two minutes and twenty seconds, and became the second most powerful solid rocket motor ever tested.
title: Giant rocket booster fired on its side
description:
On June 26, 2025, Northrop Grumman test fired its new five-segment BOLE solid rocket motor, built for future flights of NASA's Space Launch System, at its Promontory site in Utah. It burned for about two minutes and 20 seconds and produced over 4 million pounds of thrust.

facts.claim: First test firing of BOLE five-segment motor at Promontory, Utah
facts.source_quote: Northrop Grumman conducted the first test firing of its Booster Obsolescence and Life Extension (BOLE) five-segment solid rocket motor at its Promontory production and test site in Utah.

facts.claim: Fired June 26, about 2 minutes 20 seconds, 1.4 million pounds of propellant
facts.source_quote: fired Thursday, June 26, at 12:25 PM MDT (18:25 UTC) and lasted for close to two minutes and 20 seconds, burning over 1.4 million pounds of propellant.

facts.claim: Over 4 million pounds of thrust; 763 channels of data
facts.source_quote: the booster generated over 4 million pounds of thrust upon ignition and burned for approximately two minutes and 20 seconds. Sensors monitored hundreds of parameters using 763 channels of data

facts.claim: Second most powerful solid motor ever tested
facts.source_quote: The BOLE DM-1 motor turned out to be the second most powerful solid rocket motor ever tested

facts.claim: Mounted on its side, held by concrete block
facts.source_quote: The motor, mounted on its side, was held down by a large concrete block, which prevents it from moving forward.
